title: I made a tiny desktop pixel farm with Claude. The pixel art and sound effects come from scripts, not image models
author: Rockcue
selftext:
I'm a solo dev and I just released a small desktop pixel farm made with Claude. Sharing how the AI parts worked.

  
What it is: Kongsim Farm, a tiny cozy farm that sits in a corner of your screen while you work. Click to plant, harvest when it's grown, and hand crops to visiting animal merchants. 16 crops across four seasons, 9 merchants, decorating and expanding the farm, a farm photo feature. Mouse only, and you can pin the window on top of other windows. Windows and macOS, fully offline, saves stay on your computer.

  
How AI was used (also listed on the itch page):

• Game code: written with Claude. Engine is Godot.

• Pixel art: Claude wrote the scripts that draw the pixel art, so the sprites come out of code rather than an image model.

• Sound effects: same approach, scripts that generate the SFX.

• In-game text and the English translation.

  
What I did by hand: every design decision, and I reviewed every screen myself.

  
Happy to go into the workflow in the comments: how the art scripts are set up, what needed fixing by hand, and so on.



Pricing: $1 or more, pay what you want. No ads, no wait timers, no cash shop.

  
[https://yaa-corp.itch.io/kongsim-farm](https://yaa-corp.itch.io/kongsim-farm)

  
Curious whether anyone else here generates pixel art from code instead of image models, and how you keep the style consistent.
